evidence: CreateProjectUseCase.execute, CreateTaskUseCase.execute and CreateUserUseCase.execute each contain `Math.random().toString(36).substring(2, 11)`, so the ID generation rule is copied in three places.

AssignTaskUseCase.execute, CreateTaskUseCase.execute, MarkTaskDoneUseCase.execute and the tasks.map callback in ListTasksUseCase.execute each map the same 7 task fields (id, projectId, title, description, dueDate, status, assignedToUserId) by hand.
dtos.ts: CreateTaskResponse, AssignTaskResponse and MarkTaskDoneResponse have identical fields, and ListTasksResponse.tasks repeats them inline; there is no single shared task type.

ListTasksUseCase.execute uses taskRepository.findByProjectIdAndStatus or findByProjectIdAndAssignee for a single filter, but filters `t.status === request.status && t.assignedToUserId === request.assigneeId` in memory when both are set.

CreateUserUseCase builds `const user: User = { id, name }` as a plain object, while CreateProjectUseCase uses `new ProjectEntity(...)` and CreateTaskUseCase uses `new TaskEntity(..., 'todo')`, setting the starting status in the application layer.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module covers one concern, the application use cases for projects, users and tasks, but it repeats rules and mappings that should each live in one place. The ID generation rule is copied in three use cases. The Task-to-response mapping is written out four times. dtos.ts declares the same Task response shape four times instead of sharing one type. ListTasksUseCase uses the repository's filtered queries for single filters but filters in memory when both filters are set, which bypasses the repository query abstraction. Entity construction is also inconsistent: CreateUserUseCase builds a plain object literal while the other create use cases use ProjectEntity and TaskEntity, and CreateTaskUseCase sets the starting status 'todo' itself instead of leaving it to the entity.
